$comment: Money-path PR assurance configuration, read from the default branch by .github/workflows/money-pr-assurance.yml. See docs/runbooks/money-pr-assurance.md. Changing this file is itself a money-path change.

moneyKeywords.$comment: A changed file is a money path when its path contains one of these words anywhere, ignoring case and treating hyphens and underscores alike. Interface components, screens, hooks, scripts and tests count too: money logic lives in all of them. Only documentation and images (`outside`) never count. SQL files are named freely, so their changed text is searched as well (`contentPaths`) for the keywords and, as whole words or identifier parts, the money verbs in `contentWords`; other code files count when the lines they add or remove call or define a money operation (`money-pr-assurance-detect.mjs`, shared with the contract sweep), and SQL whose changed text GitHub does not return counts as money. `moneyPaths` adds money code whose path has none of the words: checkout code in the apps and shared packages, the orders API, wallet-releasing self-fulfilment, domain payment callbacks, the service-role client that money webhooks use, the hosted staging request gate, PiggyVest staging tools and the VPS cron runner. A contract test finds today's money code from what each file does and fails if any of it is missed.

headings: What could go wrong and how it is prevented

reviewers.$comment: Never trust github-actions[bot]: every workflow token, including one a pull request controls, posts as it. A Gemini family can return once its verdict comes from an identity pull-request workflows cannot use. Each reviewer's verdict counts only after the latest request, from a `requestedBy` login, that names the main branch's prompt and the full head commit.

signoffPaths.$comment: A money-path PR that also changes one of these files needs the owner's sign-off: they define the CI checks the assurance relies on.
